purpose: Regression cases for runtime Evaluator–Optimizer behavior.

cases.prompt: Evaluate a requirement document where FR-20 was incorrectly renumbered to FR-19 after the original FR-19 became OUT_OF_SCOPE. The authoritative registry preserves stable IDs.
expected: Evaluator identifies the stable-ID violation with evidence.
Finding is AUTO_FIXABLE when authoritative history is unambiguous.
Optimizer restores the established ID instead of inventing a new numbering scheme.
Candidate is re-evaluated after the fix.

cases.prompt: Two equally authoritative requirement documents conflict about whether refunds are allowed. No accepted decision resolves the conflict.
expected: Finding is HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED.
Workflow returns BLOCKED_REQUIRES_DECISION.
Optimizer does not choose one business rule on its own.

cases.prompt: An NFR says response time must be fast but no numeric target has been approved. A downstream template expects a number.
expected: Evaluator identifies the missing approved target.
Workflow does not invent a latency value.
Status is BLOCKED_REQUIRES_DECISION when the number is required for the task.

cases.prompt: Evaluate a candidate that already satisfies all in-scope criteria and repository governance.
expected: Workflow returns PASS.
No optimizer rewrite is performed merely to make stylistic changes outside scope.

cases.prompt: A candidate still has the same major correctness failure after three authorized optimization rounds.
expected: Workflow stops after the configured/default iteration limit.
Status is BLOCKED_ITERATION_LIMIT.
Remaining findings are reported instead of continuing indefinitely.

cases.prompt: During the evaluation phase the evaluator notices a broken metadata date that is unambiguously fixable.
expected: Evaluator reports the finding but does not silently edit during evaluation.
Optimizer performs the authorized fix in the optimization phase using the owning rules.
The fix is verified in a subsequent evaluation.

cases.prompt: The evaluator reports one auto-fixable metadata issue in a large accepted SRS. Nearby prose could also be rewritten for style but is not a finding.
expected: Optimizer changes only the evidence-supported finding and the smallest coherent dependencies.
Unrelated accepted requirement wording is preserved.

cases.prompt: Fixing a documentation finding would require creating or closing GitHub Issues, but the user only authorized local documentation edits.
expected: Workflow does not perform the remote mutation.
If that action is required to satisfy the requested gate, final status is BLOCKED_AUTHORIZATION.
The needed authorization is reported explicitly.

cases.prompt: The evaluator is checking a proposed batch that would update and close GitHub Issues. The evaluator has GitHub write capability available.
expected: Evaluator may read remote state as evidence but performs no remote writes during evaluation.
Mutation authority is deferred to the approved Optimizer/Executor phase.

cases.prompt: A GitHub synchronization candidate passes evaluation and proposes CREATE 2 Issues, UPDATE 1, CLOSE 1. No remote write has occurred yet.
expected: Workflow presents one complete mutation preview and stops before the first write.
One explicit human approval may authorize the entire exact previewed batch.
If the batch materially changes after approval, old approval is invalidated and a new preview/approval is required.
Remote state is verified after execution.
